articles.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
articles.dek: For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was a triumph of sorts. The hard numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s…
articles.description: For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was a triumph of sorts. The hard numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the Sunderland box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable too. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the only survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic just seven months ago. With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving one of Zion Suzuki’s uprights with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka and comfortably eliminating the defender before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to a post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches. Continue reading...

Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka and comfortably eliminating the defender before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to a post.

articles.title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
articles.dek: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They…
articles.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

articles.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
articles.dek: Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But when the momentum is against you, sometimes even a change of manager cannot stop the…
articles.description: Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But when the momentum is against you, sometimes even a change of manager cannot stop the rot. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. Palace may feel themselves unlucky, but Thomas Frank started with a defeat and his side have now lost five successive league games. For much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour for a win that lifted them three points clear of the relegation zone. Continue reading...

articles.dek: Not since the emergence of Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed…
articles.description: Not since the emergence of Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and matchwinning assist against Ipswich. That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’ Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday. Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.
